AN ACT to amend the labor law, in relation to establishing a registration
system for contractors and subcontractors engaged in public work projects in
order to better enforce existing labor laws and regulations in the public
works industry
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5994

SPONSOR: RYAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the labor law, in relation to establishing a registra-
tion system for contractors and subcontractors engaged in public work
projects in order to better enforce existing labor laws and regulations
in the public works industry

 
PURPOSE:

This legislation creates a registration system for contractors that wish
to bid on public works projects in New York. It would ensure public
works contractors do not have previous labor law violations and will
abide by New York labor laws and regulations, including prevailing wage
requirements.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Establishes a registration system for contractors and subcon-
tractors that bid on "public works" in New York. It requires that
contractors register with the Department of Labor and pay a registration
fee. Once registered, the Department of Labor will issue a certificate
of registration that must be presented to public entities when bidding
on a project. The Commissioner of Labor is empowered to suspend or
revoke a registration on a finding of wrong doing. The bill creates a
process for the finding of violations, the ability to issue penalties,
and a process for the contractor to appeal the suspension or revocation.

Section 2: Establishes the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Public works projects in New York are governed by Article 8 of the New
York Labor Law. Among other requirements, public work contractors are
required to pay "prevailing wage" on public works projects. At times,
public works contractors have been found to have violated the "prevail-
ing wage" rates and/or other provisions of the Labor Law.  Other states
with similar systems have adopted a registration system for public works
contractors to prevent bad actors from receiving contracts in the first
place. This legislation would create a registration system in New York.

This legislation would create a system whereby any contractor wishing to
bid on a public works project must register with the Department of Labor
and pay a registration fee. It would provide the Department an opportu-
nity to vet the contractor to see if they had any previous violations of
the Labor Law, and ensure only responsible contractors are allowed to
bid on New York public works projects.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-2020: A.1802;

2017-2018: A.3057-A;

2016: A.9089-A

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately, provided however, subdivisions five and six of section
220-i of the Labor Law as added by section one of this act shall take
effect one year after such date and shall apply to bids for public work
projects on or after such date.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5994A

SPONSOR: RYAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the labor law, in relation to establishing a registra-
tion system for contractors and subcontractors engaged in public work
and covered projects in order to better enforce existing labor laws and
regulations in the public works industry

 
PURPOSE:

To create a registration system for contractors that wish to bid on
contracts for public work and commence work on certain covered projects
in New York. It would ensure the contractors do not have previous labor
law violations and will abide by New York labor laws and regulations,
including prevailing wage requirements.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Sections 1-2 of the bill amend the labor law by adding a new section
220-i.

Section 1 establishes a registration system for contractors and subcon-
tractors that bid on certain covered projects in New York.  Provides
definitions for relevant terms, including "contractor, "bureau," and
"covered project."

Provides requirements for written registration prior to bidding on a
contract or commencing work on a covered project under private contract.

Requires contractor to submit documentation to the commissioner proving
workers' compensation insurance for all workers and submit a non-refund-
able registration fee.

Provides for registrations issued by the commissioner and notice and
documentation requirements in the event of an "unfit" contractor.
Establishes civil penalties for registration violations for owners and
developers, contractors, and subcontractors working on public work
and/or covered projects.

Establishes a publicly accessible online system to make available all
registrations and disclosures required by this section.

Section 2 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Construction projects subject to "prevailing wage" in New York are
governed by Article 8 of the New York Labor Law. At times, contractors
for covered projects have been found to have violated the "prevailing
wage" rates and/or other provisions of the Labor Law.  Other states with
similar systems have adopted a registration system for covered project
contractors to prevent bad actors from receiving contracts in the first
place. This legislation would create a registration system in New York.

This legislation would create a system whereby any contractor wishing to
bid on a covered project must register with the Department of Labor and
pay a registration fee. It would provide the Department an opportunity
to vet the contractor to see if they had any previous violations of the
Labor Law and ensure only responsible contractors are allowed to bid on
New York covered projects.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-2020: A.1802;

2017-2018: A.3057-A;

2016: A.9089-A

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately, provided however, subdivisions
one through six of section 220-i of the labor law as added by section
one of this act shall take effect one year after such date.

BILL NUMBER: S5994B

SPONSOR: RYAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the labor law, in relation to establishing a registra-
tion system for contractors and subcontractors engaged in public work
and covered projects in order to better enforce existing labor laws and
regulations in the public works industry

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To create a registration system for contractors that wish to bid on
contracts for public work and commence work on certain covered projects
in New York. It would ensure the contractors do not have previous labor
law violations and will abide by New York labor laws and regulations,
including prevailing wage requirements.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Sections 1-2 of the bill amend the labor law by adding a new section
220-i.

Section 1 establishes a registration system for contractors and subcon-
tractors that bid on certain covered projects in New York.

Provides definitions for relevant terms, including "contractor,"

Requires contractor to submit documentation to the commissioner proving

able registration fee.

Provides for registrations issued by the commissioner and notice and
documentation requirements in the event of an "unfit" contractor.

Establishes civil penalties for registration violations for owners and
developers, contractors, and subcontractors working on public work
and/or covered projects.

Establishes a publicly accessible online system to make available all
registrations and disclosures required by this section.

Section 2 sets the effective date.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE):

Makes technical changes and adds the term, "covered project."

Adds the workers' compensation board employer number to the contractor's
registration form provided by the commissioner.

Requires any documents, reports, or information concerning a potentially
unfit contractor be provided no more than 10 days before the hearing.


Requires owner or developer of covered projects under private contract
to ensure that any hired contractor or subcontractor is registered
pursuant to this section.

Establishes civil penalties for owners and developers, contractors, and
subcontractors working on covered projects for registration violations.

Adds subdivision 8 that requires the Department of Labor to prescribe
regulations within one hundred eighty days after the effective date.
States that subdivisions one though six of section 1 of section 220-i of
the labor law shall take effect one year after the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Construction projects subject to "prevailing wage" in New York are
governed by Article 8 of the New York Labor Law. At times, contractors
for covered projects have been found to have violated the "prevailing
wage" rates and/or other provisions of the Labor Law.  Other states with
similar systems have adopted a registration system for covered project
contractors to prevent bad actors from receiving contracts in the first
place. This legislation would create a registration system in New York.

This legislation would create a system whereby any contractor wishing to
bid on a covered project must register with the Department of Labor and
pay a registration fee. It would provide the Department an opportunity
to vet the contractor to see if they had any previous violations of the
Labor Law and ensure only responsible contractors are allowed to bid on
New York covered projects.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-2020: A.1802;

2017-2018: A.3057-A;

2016: A.9089-A

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately, provided however, subdivisions
one through six of section 220-i of the labor law as added by section
one of this act shall take effect one year after such date.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 105 Chapter 827
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 5994-C, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the labor law, in relation to establishing a regis-
        tration  system  for  contractors  and subcontractors engaged in
        public work and covered projects  in  order  to  better  enforce
        existing  labor  laws and regulations in the public works indus-
        try"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would create a new registration system for  contractors  and
subcontractors  engaged  in  public  work and covered projects performed
under private contract. A contractor could not bid  on  a  contract  for
public  work unless the contractor and all subcontractors on the project
were registered. For covered projects performed under private  contract,
the  owner  or  developer  of  the project would need to ensure that any
contractor or subcontractor hired to perform the work is registered. The
bill would require contractors and subcontractors to provide a series of
disclosures about their business and pay a registration  fee  every  two
years.  The Department of Labor (DOL) would determine whether a contrac-
tor or subcontractor is fit to register and make the  entities'  disclo-
sure  information  publicly  available in an online database. Failure to
properly register before bidding on a project or commencing  work  on  a
covered private project would result in civil penalties.
 
  I  fully  support  efforts  to  prevent taxpayer dollars from going to
unscrupulous contractors, and I agree that a central database of  infor-
mation  about  contractors and subcontractors engaged in public work and
covered projects should exist. However, I have concerns about implement-
ing the bill as drafted. I have secured an agreement with  the  Legisla-
ture to resolve these concerns and make technical changes to the bill to
make  the  registration  system efficient and useful, and to ensure that
essential State work is not delayed.
 
  Specifically, this agreement includes language clarifying that  regis-
tration  is necessary (1) at the time of bids for contractors bidding on
public work projects; (2) at the time when work commences  for  contrac-
tors and subcontractors involved in covered private projects; and (3) at
the  time  work  commences  for  subcontractors.  Further, the agreement
adjusts the unfitness determination timing to mirror existing  licensing
registrations  by  DOL and to clarify that a contractor or subcontractor
will be considered unfit if they are subject to a State or federal order
for prevailing wage violations that has not been  fully  satisfied.  The
agreement  also  adds  a new provision to address contractors or subcon-
tractors continuing work when  a  registration  lapses,  as  well  as  a
requirement  that  a monitor be appointed to oversee the work in a situ-
ation where work is on-going and a contractor or subcontractor has  been
determined  unfit. In addition to other technical changes, the effective
date of the legislation has been moved to two  years  so  that  DOL  has
sufficient time to adopt regulations and set up the registration system.
 
  On the basis of this agreement, I am pleased to sign this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______
